findings.reason: a plan whose stated preference is a deep module behind a small interface should either fold the prose buckets into the one raw-text pass or state why two identity-resolution sites cannot be avoided.
findings.text: §16's `_AuthoredProseParser` and §17's `_StructuredSectionSpanParser` are each extended to track the attributes of the enclosing section element and derive the wrapper-id-case identity, so the same rule is implemented twice, in reckon/ (core) and reckon/crew/ (crew); because it is package-private it cannot be shared across that boundary without a new public definition, which §16's interface accounting does not count.

findings.reason: the first implementation node cannot be ordered while the owner of the derivation is unsettled, so the plan must name which section lands it and reverse or drop the declared dependency.
findings.text: §16 says the hoist and extension of `section_record_id`/`section_id_candidates` into `reckon/_plan_html.py` is its own change, while §16's closing sentence declares "This section depends on §17 for section identity" and §17 is the consumer that applies "the extended `section_record_id`"; the two sections each name the other as their prerequisite.

findings.reason: this is a stale cross-reference rather than a design defect, corrected by naming the recogniser's post-§17 home once.
findings.text: §18 describes the store as answering its neighbouring question "through `landed_section_ids`", but §17 moves that recogniser out of `reckon/_store.py` into `reckon/_plan_html.py` (and §16 currently imports it `from reckon._store` at reckon/crew/plan_review.py:60), so the sections disagree about where the one card recogniser lives.

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — §16 extends `_AuthoredProseParser` (reckon/crew/plan_review.py:162) and §17 extends `_StructuredSectionSpanParser` (reckon/_plan_html.py:44) so each independently records the enclosing `<section>` element's attributes to resolve wrapper-id identity, spreading one derivation over two raw-text walks in two different packages.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §16 locates the home and extension of `section_record_id` in reckon/_plan_html.py, yet its closing sentence declares §16 depends on §17 for the identity §17 itself consumes from that hoisted copy, leaving the derivation's owner unresolved between the two sections.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1476, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §16 states it adds no public definition and retires none (the digest and the prose walk keep their names, and the coverage predicate stays private because its consumers share the package), §17 names one addition (`plan_headings`) and one move (`landed_section_ids`, family unchanged), §18 names one addition and one private retirement, and no CLI option, MCP view or refusal family is added (§16 reuses the existing `plan-review-missing` family and names the uncovered sections in its detail).
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the design extends the mechanisms it names rather than proposing new machinery: `section_record_id`/`section_id_candidates` (reckon/crew/routing.py:215,234), `_StructuredSectionSpanParser`/`structured_section_spans`/`landed_section_ids` (reckon/_plan_html.py:44,94; reckon/_store.py:1034), `plan_fingerprint`/`_fingerprint_forms`/`read_plan_review`/`list_plan_reviews` (reckon/crew/plan_review.py:368,598,618,668), `_plan_remaining_sections` (reckon/crew/promotion.py:7236), `_implementable_section_ids` (reckon/doccheck.py:1014), the two `c-run-` owners (reckon/crew/promotion.py:7209, reckon/crew/plan_review.py:123) and the AST census in reckon/interface_counts.py; I opened each and confirmed it exists where cited.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the one new public layer, `plan_headings`, is justified in §17's own text by five cross-package consumers over a parser that stays private, and the retained `structured_section_spans` carries a distinct spans-only contract rather than duplicating it.
